$comment:
Urlencoded edition-to-lane case table, shared byte-for-byte by the three engines that build an
OpenAPI application/x-www-form-urlencoded request body: openbindings-go/formats/openapi,
openapi-client/go, and openapi-client/typescript/src (which openbindings-ts/packages/openapi
re-exports).

WHAT THIS TABLE GUARDS. Which of two paths an urlencoded property takes:

  style path    RFC6570 form expansion of the property value (an object explodes into its own
                members), per the Encoding Object style/explode/allowReserved fields
  content path  the property value encoded as one unit under the Encoding Object contentType,
                whose default for an object is application/json

THE SELECTOR IS PRESENCE, AND IT IS EDITION-INDEPENDENT. A property whose Encoding Object writes
an explicit style, explode or allowReserved takes the style path; one that writes none of the
three takes the content path. That holds on ALL EIGHT accepted editions, which is why the
"partition" map below is uniform -- ITS UNIFORMITY IS THE ASSERTION, not a placeholder. 3.0.4 and
the 3.1 line state the predicate in their own text. 3.0.0-3.0.3 state no lane-selection rule at
all, and reach the same behaviour through their OWN section 4.1: "Tooling which supports OAS 3.0
SHOULD be compatible with all OAS 3.0.* versions. The patch version SHOULD NOT be considered by
tooling, making no distinction between 3.0.0 and 3.0.1 for example." 3.0.4 is a 3.0.* version and
says outright that with all three fields absent "Encoding is to be based on contentType alone", so
only the content path is consistent with all five 3.0-line texts read under section 2's
per-edition discipline. Each cell's "basis" carries the passage for its own edition.

HISTORY, BECAUSE THIS TABLE'S 3.0-LINE ROWS USED TO SAY THE OPPOSITE. Until 2026-08-17 the three
engines carried a legacyOpenAPIFormEncoding(3.0.0|3.0.1|3.0.2|3.0.3) predicate that routed those
four editions' control-free properties onto the style path. It was the only patch-version-keyed
behavioural switch in any of them; it silently discarded an explicitly written encoding.contentType
(and with it the field name that contentType governed), collided sibling field names, and refused
at dispatch for values the artifact had fully declared. It was removed by the ruling in
design/openapi-30-urlencoded-default-lane-ruling.md, and the openapi family specifications section 2 now
states the patch-uniformity reading once for the whole family.

DO NOT re-derive the answer from the sentence "the default serialization strategy of such
properties is described in the Encoding Object's style property as form". That sentence is present
in 3.0.0, 3.0.1, 3.0.2, 3.0.3 AND 3.1.0, and absent from 3.0.4, 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 (reproduce: node
corpus-lab/scripts/strip-oas-html.mjs --count "the default serialization strategy of such
properties is described in the Encoding Object.s style property as form" -> 1/1/1/1/0/1/0/0). It
partitions nothing, and a doc comment in all three engines once cited it as though it did.

Each case is rendered as a WHOLE OpenAPI document and loaded through each engine's own loader, so
the table exercises the shipped path rather than a hand-built typed model. Every cell was observed
in all three engines before it was written down; the authority quotations in "basis" were verified
against corpus-lab/authorities/texts/openapi/oas at the digests recorded in
corpus-lab/OPENAPI-RUNTIME.md.

Shape of every case: one urlencoded request body whose schema is
{type: object, properties: {address: {type: object, properties: {street: {type: string}}}}},
invoked with {"address": {"street": "main st"}}. An object-valued property is used because it is
the smallest value whose two paths emit different bytes; a primitive emits the same bytes on both
paths and would guard nothing -- for primitives, and for the %20/+ escaper boundary the two paths
draw differently, see urlencoded-escaper-cases.json and urlencoded-content-lane-cases.json.

cases.name: 3.0.0|no-encoding
cases.basis: No RFC6570-style control is written. Edition 3.0.0 states no lane-selection rule of its own: its §4.7.15.1 style/explode/allowReserved descriptions condition nothing on contentType, and §4.7.14.4 says only that "the default serialization strategy of such properties is described in the Encoding Object’s style property as form" — a sentence present verbatim in 3.1.0 as well, so it partitions nothing. The rule that governs this cell is THIS edition’s own §4.1: "Tooling which supports OAS 3.0 SHOULD be compatible with all OAS 3.0.* versions. The patch version SHOULD NOT be considered by tooling, making no distinction between 3.0.0 and 3.0.1 for example." 3.0.4 is a 3.0.* version, so the whole 3.0 line takes ONE behaviour, and 3.0.4 §4.7.15.1.2 fixes which one: with all three fields absent, "Encoding is to be based on contentType alone". Running the style path here would contradict 3.0.4 read under its own text, which the openapi family specifications §2 equally requires, so the content path is the only reading consistent with all five 3.0-line texts.

cases.name: 3.0.0|style
cases.basis: An explicitly written style selects the RFC6570-style path, on every accepted edition. 3.0.4 §4.7.15.1.2 and the 3.1 line’s §4.8.15.1 / §4.8.15.1.2 each state that an explicitly defined control makes contentType ignored; 3.0.0–3.0.3 state no lane-selection rule of their own and reach the same behaviour through their own §4.1 patch-uniformity instruction, as the no-control cells of this table set out. The predicate is PRESENCE, not truthiness: an allowReserved: false or explode: false that merely restates the field’s own default is still an explicit value.
